intended_object: The disc automorphism z ↦ u·(z − a)/(1 − ā z), where |u| = 1 and |a| < 1, viewed as an isometric bijection (an element of the isometry group) of the Poincaré disc with its hyperbolic metric. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation: The definition starts from `unitDiscStandardAutomorphismEquiv u a`, which is the Möbius map `unitDiscMoebius a`, given by z ↦ (z − a)/(1 − conj(a)·z), followed by rotation by u. Its inverse is the Möbius map centred at −a followed by rotation by u⁻¹, so the map really is a bijection. The definition then turns this map into an `IsometryEquiv` of `PoincareDisc`, using the library's proof that it preserves hyperbolic distance. `PoincareDisc` is the unit disc carrying the hyperbolic metric, and the reinterpretation maps between the two types are the identity. So the underlying function is exactly u(z − a)/(1 − āz), which matches the docstring and the standard formula for disc automorphisms. The construction is about the Poincaré disc itself, so it is not set in a narrower generality than its natural one. Mathlib has no Poincaré-disc metric and no bundled disc automorphisms as isometries (it only has the upper half-plane metric), so there is no Mathlib counterpart.
